evidence: The authoritative workbook Quality Checks!D29 forbids duplicate/subsumed criteria; the internal annotation permits sharing a flow, not double credit ownership. Current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:13 further requires preserving independently useful observations. Two concrete conflicts remain. (1) .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:605 (hro_claim_identity, weight 1.0) adds claimedActorId, claimedRole AND claimedTier and requires an otherwise valid request to have the same result as omission. The same file:614 (hro_claim_approval_economics, weight 0.5) adds claimedBand, claimedTier AND claimedCommittedCents, again requiring the optional claims to be ignored and explicitly failing rejection merely for their presence. The valid-approval acceptance of claimedTier is therefore the same observable graded twice; no ownership/fallback rule isolates it. Public environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md:380-383 requires ignoring these keys but does not make ignoring one key two independent outcomes. (2) tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:110 explicitly limits hro_offer_identity to creation/saved identity and gives later unusual-ID approval/rescission/revision routing separate owners; lines119 and128 separately own unusual-ID approval and rescission. But tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:34 commands, after performing approval and subsequent actions on unusual IDs, "If ID routing fails, retain that failure in hro_offer_identity". This assigns a later routing miss to the already-proven creation outcome and conflicts with both its criterion boundary and prompt.md:9 independent scoring. Counterexamples below establish textual scoring defects; no provider run or empirical judge deduction was executed. Static hash verification matched all 69 frozen task/rule files and the current policy to the manifest for adb13696bfe3e6c71690adc5c6af2002d5f107a10751c348ba8bc0f5401600b1. No raw-evidence index was present, and this report does not claim an Oracle, model, portal or full-judge result. Reviewed non-defects: ordinary positive controls, refusal plus unchanged financial state, and shared setup are coherent outcomes under policy; the explicit separation of feedback/enforcement, arithmetic/history, anonymous write families, same-target concurrency and mobile operability/visual composition generally preserves credit. Tried seed-only/no-op storage as a broken-pass candidate: the required unique UI creation plus independent Auditor readback prevents that witness by the written gate. Tried conforming nonmodal editors, stacked/scrollable breakdowns, native date controls, opaque routes and a common bootstrap response: the wording permits these alternatives; no fully conforming-app false-fail is asserted for them.
counterexample: A: An otherwise functional app ignores all optional keys except that a validator rejects the presence of claimedTier on an authorized approval. Omission controls approve normally; role enforcement, stored actor, band, commitment and headroom are correct. The same isolated claimedTier defect fails both hro_claim_identity and hro_claim_approval_economics, even though claimedBand/claimedCommittedCents protection works. B: An app correctly stores and retrieves unusual requisition/offer IDs and every entered field but forgets URL encoding only in its approval handler; ordinary-ID approval works. P1 creation/readback satisfies hro_offer_identity, while hro_offer_id_lifecycle correctly fails. Repeating that same routing miss in P4 makes prompt.md:34 assign failure to hro_offer_identity as well, erasing independently valid creation credit. These are source-level partial-app counterexamples, not claimed executed mutations.
suggested_fix: Give claimedTier acceptance/authority exactly one criterion owner (for example retain it in identity and test approval economics with only claimedBand/claimedCommittedCents), and change P4 to record each routing failure only against its actual action-specific owner while preserving saved creation/readback credit; explicitly assign revision-ID routing if needed and keep the ordinary-ID fallback for unrelated economic outcomes.
